## 2026-10-23 — hard-killed lane builds clean up after themselves

Spend served the owner's 2026-10-23 pick "Hard-kill watcher (Recommended)", under the priority of the day (nana working the same for both seats in terminal mode); it carried into the artifact priority as authorized work. A hard kill of pi-worker (a pi seat's Esc, a closed terminal, a desk stop, a bash timeout) left the temp folder with the carried Claude settings, the capture folder, the lane lock and a running builder, and the build ledger had no end record.

**The change.** Right after pi-worker makes its lane temp folder it starts a detached watcher through a one-shot hop (`packages/nana-pack/lib/lane-watcher.mjs`, `lane-watcher-child.mjs`). When pi-worker dies hard, the watcher ends the recorded builder's process group off Windows, only if that pid still belongs to a process started no later than the record (R-2726); removes the lane's temp files; writes the missing `stopped` end record (R-2725); and releases the lane lock only when it still names pi-worker and no recorded builder may still run (R-2722, R-2727). A second lane in the same temp folder is untouched (R-2728). `pidAlive` moved to process-tree.mjs, the lock release to `lib/lane-lock.mjs`, the end-record assembly to build-records.mjs, and the tests' `killWorkerTree` to a shared test module. Rows R-2720 to R-2728.

**Seat decisions.** In `docs/reviews/hard-kill-watcher-2026-10-23/must-meet.md`: a gate lane (pi-watchdog runs inside every pi-review); the three-lens attack adopted (the start-time check, the lock rule, two lanes, the leader shape, deterministic waits, the watcher's cwd, the helper moves).

**Builds.** Two. Build 1, 0233a934 (larger), built the lane; its locked full suite: 218 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP. The seat found the builder's own mutation table committed under the package's tests folder, and R-2727's cmd.exe half unpinned (removing it kept the check green); build 2, 65b43672 (small), removed both stray files and widened R-2727's check.

**Evidence.** 22 of 22 wrong-code pairs red at 0233a934 and 23 of 23 at 65b43672, pair 23 pinning the cmd.exe half (`seat-mutate-output-65b43672.txt`). The seat's probes on macOS: a SIGKILL of pi-worker alone, of a wrapper's parent-pid tree, a finished build and two lanes in one temp folder all ended clean, with no watcher left. The independent check at 65b43672 (`independent-check-65b43672.md`) ran 51 early kills, 14 tree kills during startup, 20 SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL runs and pid-reuse decoys: no MUST; its two SHOULDs are known limits.

**Notes folded in.** The plan's and the independent check's limits are FEAT-006 lines; FEAT-006's lane-temp leftover line and FEAT-031's build-report leftover line close, and the build-records `no end` line narrows. review-round's private pid-liveness copy is a FEAT-007 line. report-at-land's final-review notes are FEAT-039 and FEAT-031 lines.

## 2026-10-23 — no carried Claude settings left in the temp folder

Spend served the owner's 2026-10-23 pick "Lane temp cleanup", under the current priority's line that nana works the same for both seats. In lane mode pi-worker copied the user Claude settings, key included, into a temp folder before it refused a review option, and left the folder. A stop signal in the first tenth of a second left it too, once with the lane lock. The Claude builder test read a caller's exported `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and three checks failed on such a machine.

**The change.** `packages/nana-pack/bin/pi-worker.mjs` refuses review options first, in both modes, before it reads the brief, the roster or the Claude settings or writes any temp file (R-2691). In lane mode it registers no-op SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP listeners just before the temp folder and keeps them, so a signal in the start-up window queues and reaches the watchdog's stop path (R-2693). It ignores a closed standard-error pipe in lane mode, which had crashed it mid-build. R-2692 pins every handled exit to an empty temp folder. `worker-claude.test.mjs` and `build-records.test.mjs` clear `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and a decoy pins it.

**Seat decisions.** In `docs/reviews/lane-temp-cleanup-2026-10-23/must-meet.md`: the gate ladder on the owner's word, though AGENTS.md's letter reads ordinary; a pi seat's ordinary stop (Esc, a closed terminal, a desk stop) named as the common hard kill that still leaves the folder and a running builder (M-1); the closed-pipe fix (S-1); a missing-brief run in R-2691 (S-2); a pi build in R-2693 (S-3). The owner put a cleanup watcher for hard kills in the queue, and said yes to removing the planning machine's leftover fixture folders: the seat removed 34 by name, each checked to name a test fixture (one more than the 33 counted at planning, the same kind).

**Builds.** Three. Build 1, e5bf20ed (larger), built the lane; its locked full suite: 216 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP. The seat found a stray committed copy of the suite output (F1); build 2, f3df8596 (small), removed it. The land reviewer's round 1 sent the lane back: the listeners sat before three reads that can hang, so a SIGTERM to pi-worker no longer ended it there, where main's did. Build 3, 07d692b3 (larger), moved the trust check, the user Claude settings read and the HEAD read ahead of the listeners (R-2694); its locked full suite: 216 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP.

**Evidence.** 18 of 18 wrong-code pairs turn a check red at f3df8596 (`seat-mutate-output-f3df8596.txt`), and 21 of 21 with V5 to V7 at 07d692b3 (`seat-mutate-output-07d692b3.txt`). The independent check found nothing material (`independent-check-a3293dc4.md`); its two notes are FEAT-006 lines. ## 2026-10-23 — the install check starts a real lane build

Spend served the owner's 2026-10-23 pick "Builder launch in install check", under the current priority's install-and-hooks line. The install check started pi-review but never pi-worker, so a broken builder launcher could reach a seat unseen.

**The change.** After doctor, `packages/nana-setup/lib/install-check.mjs` points the temporary home's roster builder at the review fixture's test model and adds the fixture to pi's extensions. It then starts one offline lane build through each installed pi-worker launcher (`pi-worker` by path off Windows; `pi-worker (cmd)` and `pi-worker (sh)` on Windows), each from its own linked worktree of the review repository on a `feat/` branch. `judgePiWorker` passes a line only when the run exits 0 in time; its output ends in the fixture's answer and verdict lines; the fixture's record holds the rendered builder preamble, the whole brief, the writing tag and the worker role; the build ledger holds exactly one accepted start and end pair for the lane; and the lane lock is released. A failed run names its exit status and pi's first output line, or the launcher's last stderr line. The review's launch switch moved into a shared `launchInstalled` helper, and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` joined the override list. The values are sealed in `PI_BUILD` (R-2681 to R-2687, one pin).

**Seat decisions.** In `docs/reviews/install-check-builder-2026-10-23/must-meet.md`: an ordinary lane, since it changes the install check alone; the session-folder variable overridden (M-1); the offline value as the build's one environment addition (M-2); the build after doctor, so no later row reads the edited roster (S-1); stub readers that behave as pi-worker's do (S-2); a config that cannot be edited fails as a launch (S-3); PowerShell left for a later lane.

Pair 34, the build before the hook rows, survives, because the test stub's roster notice is fixed; it is a FEAT-015 known bug. Pair 32 turns the file red by a throw before its named case. Spend served the owner's 2026-10-22 power-mode pick, "One shared rename-retry and one process-kill helper replace 3 and 8 copies, plus a rule to reuse helpers." Builders had copied the kill and rename code lane by lane, and the copies had drifted apart.

**The change.** `packages/nana-pack/lib/process-tree.mjs` holds the one tree kill, in a waiting form (`killProcessTree`) and a no-wait form (`killProcessTreeNoWait`): off Windows it signals the process group once, SIGKILL by default; on Windows it starts `taskkill /T /F /PID` without a shell; a pid that is not a whole number above 1 signals nothing; a caller's fallback runs only when the signal or taskkill fails, and no fallback error escapes. Six copies now call it: the install relay, post-edit's checker kill, the test runner, the mutation runner, pi-watchdog and the bench runner. `packages/nana-pack/lib/rename-retry.mjs` holds the one rename retry (EPERM, EBUSY and EACCES on every platform, three attempts 20 ms apart), used by project setup and the review-text store. `packages/nana-pack/lib/tree-kill-scan.mjs` names any new kill copy in mapped production code outside four declared exceptions, and the suite fails on one. The builder preamble and the shipped rulings gain the reuse rule. Rows R-2656 to R-2663.

**Seat decisions.** In `docs/reviews/shared-helpers-2026-10-23/must-meet.md`: one gate lane; the rename codes unified (D1); the pid-alive checks left out; the pairs judged by main's runner, because the lane changes the runner's own kill.

**Builds.** Two. Build 1, e2225246 (larger), built the lane. The seat found the scan and its exception list inside the runtime kill module, against the must-meet's N9 (F1); build 2, 77cba752 (small), moved them to their own module.

**Evidence.** 26 of 26 wrong-code pairs turn a check red at 77cba752 on main's runner (`seat-mutate-output-77cba752.txt`); two of them make their test file throw before the named check, a FEAT-033 known bug. The Windows-only pair 23 is red on a scratch CI branch (`seat-win-pairs-77cba752.txt`). The macOS install check passes every item (`install-check-77cba752.txt`). The independent check found no material problem (`independent-check-77cba752.md`). CI at 77cba752 passed on all three suite legs and both install-check legs. Build 2's locked full suite: 216 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP.

The flaky-test lane's two final-review notes, which came after its LAND, are FEAT-031 lines here. ## 2026-10-21 — on Windows the gate reads Git Bash's `/tmp` and `/c/` spellings as Git for Windows mounts them

Spend served the current priority's line on every hook working on Windows. Since rm-outside-asks landed on 2026-10-20, a headless Windows builder or reviewer running `rm -f /tmp/out.txt` in Git Bash was blocked, because the gate read `/tmp` as `C:\tmp`.

**The change.** For pi's bash tool on win32, `gitBashPath` reads `/tmp` and `/tmp/…` as the folder TMP names, or TEMP when TMP is unset or empty, and `/<letter>` and `/<letter>/…` as that drive, upper-cased. It runs after `path.posix.normalize` and leaves `//`-led and backslash spellings alone. It applies to rm targets and to `cd` and `pushd` folders, before the unchanged containment rule, so the shared temp-folder rule still decides. A TMP at a drive root, the home folder or above it still asks. PowerShell, macOS and Linux read paths as before. nana-gate passes `process.platform` and the live `process.env`. Rows R-2490 to R-2497 in FEAT-010. The plan adversary's four SHOULDs shaped it: exact-path asserts for the lookalikes, collapsing `..` before the translation, a cd-with-drive case on the Windows leg, and a draft pull request so the Windows leg runs at all.

**Evidence.** The seat's eleven wrong-code pairs are 11 of 11 red on macOS (`seat-mutate-output-*.txt`). Pair (j), nana-gate passing no platform or env, rests on the Windows leg, where R-2495 to R-2497 run against the real handler and Git Bash's own `cygpath`. The independent check found no material problem over 52 honest spellings with an emulated win32 path module (`independent-check.md`). Its SHOULD, a `..` after a link in the temp folder, is a known limit; build 5 corrected three wording claims it showed were not always true. The macOS install check passes locally (17 PASS). CI figures are in the review brief.

**Carried to HANDOFF.** One Landed line; four residual lines dropped (the Git Bash `/tmp` block, the `/tmp` wording, the rm-inside comment and the README's git wording, all fixed here); ten new residual lines (eight known limits and two floor gaps for Git Bash spellings).

**Seat items from other lanes.**
- win-leg-flakes (round 1 final review, LAND on 28dae7c4): one residual line on R-2483 and the linked Claude folder flake, the unused export added to the install-child line, and its session entry's residual count corrected to seven known limits and three cause-audit findings.

## 2026-10-21 — the four first-try Windows CI failures: the install check retries a failed pi-subagents install with a NOTE per attempt, and three test limits come from measured runs

Spend served the current priority's appetite line on a Windows CI runner and the fixes it finds. The Windows leg has blocked release since 2026-10-19, and four first attempts failed in about 13 hours before passing on a re-run, one of them a main push.

**Causes.** The planner read each failing log and 16 passing Windows legs (`docs/reviews/win-leg-flakes-2026-10-21/must-meet.md`). stale-copies killed a slow install at its 5-second child limit; pack-config-utf16 gave a cold PowerShell the shared 15 seconds; pi-launch-limits measured a correct stop at 6,714 ms against a 5,000 ms bound; the main push's `npm install pi-subagents` exited 1 and the check kept only pi's wrapper line, so npm's own error was lost. The fifth signature, stale-copies' linked Claude folder case, stays unexplained.

**The change.** The install check retries a failed pi-subagents install up to three times, five seconds apart, prints `NOTE pi-subagents attempt n of 3 failed — <npm's code line>` for each failure, and never retries a timeout or a launch error (R-2480, R-2481, R-2486). stale-copies gives its install children 20 seconds and keeps 5 for hooks (R-2482), and its R-1761 failure line now carries the hook run's status, signal, time and unavailable lines (R-2483). pi-launch-limits' bound is the limit plus the settle window plus 3.5 seconds, below the relay's 8-second backstop (R-2484). pack-config-utf16 launches PowerShell through a helper with 60 seconds (R-2485). Rows R-2480 to R-2486 in FEAT-031. The adversary's two MUSTs shaped the plan: a 5-second margin would have hidden a relay that lost its deadline, and a value-only pin would have passed with the old timeout still at the call site.

**Evidence.** The seat's twelve wrong-code pairs are 12 of 12 red at 72df3508, including a relay with its deadline removed, which still fails R-2020 to R-2022 under the 7.5-second bound (`seat-mutate-output-72df3508.txt`). Two meta-runs are deterministic proof without a loaded runner: a preload that slows each legacy-home install by 6 seconds turns main's stale-copies red and the lane's green, and a preload that makes the stale-copies checker fail inside the linked Claude folder hook shows the new detail. The macOS install check passes locally (17 PASS). The first Windows leg failed the new slow-install file because it passed nothing on Windows, where both its checks skipped; build 4 made the hook-detail check run there. CI figures are in the review brief.

**Carried to HANDOFF.** One Landed line; the old flake line rewritten as its outcome; ten residual lines (seven known limits, three cause-audit findings left out of scope); a Next item to count first-try Windows failures over the next 20 runs.

**Seat items from other lanes.**
- frontier-first (round 1 final review, LAND on bc529014): three residual lines — the dropped Provenance label ask's three known limits restored, the read window's unpinned edge, and the CRLF byte at the edge.
## 2026-10-21 — HANDOFF opens with its live sections, and the frontier checker reports a live section after the archive, one that ends past a default read, and a file over that read

Spend served the current priority (both seats in terminal mode) and the owner's 2026-10-16 question about a cold agent picking up a project from its files. The owner approved the lane on 2026-10-21 with the seat's slate.

**Why.** `HANDOFF.md` had grown to 1,068 lines and 334,327 bytes, with Next at line 1022. pi's read tool stops at 51,200 bytes or 2,000 lines (`dist/core/tools/truncate.js:10-11` in pi 1.0.2; pi 1.3.0 keeps both), so a pi seat that read the file at startup saw only Landed lines. Claude Code's Read refused it whole (262,144 bytes and 25,000 tokens by default).

**The change.** The seat reordered the file in the plan commit: header, Where things stand, Next, Open for the owner, Landed, Carried residuals. The 153 Landed lines dated 2026-09-18 to 2026-10-20 moved verbatim to the entry below this one (seat check: every moved line found verbatim, 0 missing); the Carried residuals are byte-identical except three stale clauses (two Windows "never ran" clauses, which the Windows log at 6a18aa36 disproves, and the pipe-narrowing ask the owner closed on 2026-10-21). Stale Next and Open lines were rewritten: the spent queue, the ended attention-limit trial, the overdue writing verdict, three Windows asks merged into one blocking ask, a stray-process ask with no process, and two asks closed by rulings. The builder (pi, small lane, two sessions) added three report kinds to `packages/nana-pack/bin/nana-frontier.mjs`: `file-size`, `section-order` and `read-window`, with the window values as sealed contract values in `lib/frontier-config.mjs`. Rows R-2470 to R-2473 in FEAT-002; R-2473 pins this repo's own file in order.

**Evidence.** `frontier.test.mjs` 51 pass at e8096fd4, every new check red on 363df471. On main's file the checker now reports three read-window findings (Where things stand ends at byte 322,874, Next at 327,130, Open for the owner at 334,326); on the restructured file it reports only the word budget and the file size. The seat's ten wrong-code pairs are 10 of 10 red (`seat-mutate-output-e8096fd4.txt`). Three existing checks changed because the new kind made them false: the `current` golden entry gains its three section-order lines, the frozen 2026-10-06 rewrite now reports exactly three section-order findings (R-877's evidence title swapped), and the frozen pre-rewrite file reports 15 findings, not 12.

**Also this session.** The writing trial's day-14 after-measure ran three days late: 14 of 16 reports put the verdict first (target 90%; baseline 0 of 32), 2% long sentences (target 8%; baseline 31%), new HANDOFF lines 11.6% long (target 11%; baseline 42%), no banned word. The owner adopted the rule (`docs/reviews/writing-trial-2026-10-04/after.md`). The owner also said yes to known bugs per feature and to a forward-only owner-name scrub, and the seat deleted 92,773 old test folders from the macOS temp folder with the owner's word (one refused for permissions).

**Carried to HANDOFF.** One Landed line; nine known-limit lines; the queue and the new asks.

## 2026-10-21 — capabilities get an optional kind, deliverables, needs, binds and a retirement line, checked by the tree checker, kept by the lift, shown in the outline and named by the tree movement report

Spend served the current priority's appetite line on the requirements tree. The owner's team, working with the product ledger, proposed that capabilities follow the product's steps and artifacts: product capabilities as stages with tangible deliverables, constraint capabilities that apply to every stage. The seat trial-fitted the design against four product ledgers; it fit the deliverables idea everywhere and the stage idea only in parts. The owner adopted it with five amendments: a constraint names the stages it binds and carries one tested row per bound stage; a deliverable is a row under the feature that produces it, with a derived consumer and its check; product capabilities are ordered stages only where a step needs an earlier stage's checked artifact; a feature lives at its main deliverable's stage; every field stays optional, and old capability IDs retire with named successors.

**Placement test.** Before any regroup, two independent placers (two model lineages) placed one product's 20 newest rows by intent and by stage. They agreed on 100 percent of capabilities and 95 percent of features on both trees, so stage placement was not 15 points better and no project's tree is regrouped. Existing trees gain the fields in place.

**The change.** `scripts/requirements-tree.mjs` reads five optional lines in a capability's own span (heading to next heading, outside fences, any order): `Kind:` (exactly `product` or `constraint`), `Deliverables:`, `Needs:`, `Binds:` and `Retired:`. `Deliverables:`, `Needs:` and `Binds:` count only on a capability with `Kind:`; on a kindless capability they stay prose, so a flat ledger's `Needs: a database` lifts and checks as before. The checker reports a bad kind or a repeated field line (R-2441); a deliverable token that is not a live row homed under the capability, or is listed twice (R-2442; an untested or planned deliverable is a gap, not a problem); a constraint capability with no `Retired:` line lacking exactly one `Binds:` line of live product capabilities, and `Binds:` on a product capability (R-2443); a need that is not an earlier live product capability, so no cycle can form (R-2444); and a retirement whose successor is missing, itself or retired, or which carries stage fields or a live feature (R-2445). The outline lists each read field after the capability's Parent line, and the outlines at c4332ecb, 4b3846ec and 5548d4c2 render unchanged (R-2446). The lift keeps each field line under its capability (R-2440, a guard). `scripts/requirements-moved.mjs` prints a `capabilities:` section for feature moves between capabilities, field changes compared as parsed lists, and capabilities at one revision only; its output is byte-identical otherwise (R-2447). The requirements skill, the shared organization seed (CAP-90 stays kindless) and this ledger's organization notes describe the format.

The install check passes on macOS and Windows. The Windows leg's log is ci-windows-f3331b06.log in the lane's review folder. ## 2026-10-20 — the pipe check asks only when a pipe's masked exit status can reach a git commit, and knows git.exe, any letter case and a path to git

Spend served the current priority's hook line: every hook working in both seats on macOS and Windows, here the shared verifier-pipe predicate behind the Claude Code PreToolUse hook and pi's nana-gate. On main any live pipe before a git commit asked, even where a `;`, a newline or a background `&` discarded the pipeline's status: `git status --short | head -3; git commit -m done` asked in Claude Code and was blocked in a headless pi session. The plan's adversary counted 402 asking commands among 2,820 unique local commands with a pipe and "commit" over 8 days. Main also missed git written `git.exe`, in another letter case, behind a path or as one quoted word (13 of the plan's 14 spelling cases gave no reason), and it asked on `my-git commit`.

**The change.** Only `packages/nana-pack/lib/pipe-guard.mjs` changes behaviour; nana-gate.ts and verifier-hook.mjs still call `verifierPipeReason(command, dialect)`. The commit finder takes `git` or `git.exe` in any letter case after the text start, whitespace, ``; & | ( ) { } ` ``, `/` or `\`, so `legit`, `my-git` and `git-lfs` do not match. The status reader scans each pipeline once from its first pipe. `&&`, `||`, a following bash `then` or `do`, bash `$?` or `${?}` in the next command, any bash `wait` after a backgrounded pipeline, PowerShell `$?`, PowerShell `$LASTEXITCODE` after a native last stage, and bash errexit live at the pipeline read the status; a closer, `fi`, `done` or `esac` after a separator is passed over. A `;`, a top-level line break or a bash background `&` discards the status. A line break after any `|` or `|&`, an escaped line break (bash backslash, PowerShell backtick) and a line break inside quotes or here-strings do not. A bash comment ends at its line break. An unquoted backslash hides only an operator, quote, space or line break after it, so `\git` stays git, and `<<\EOF` is a quoted heredoc delimiter. errexit opens after `{`, `then`, `do`, `(` and `$(`, and a `set +e` inside `(` or `$(` does not reach the outer command. A bash double quote closes after an even run of backslashes. Two live-text exposures show `"$?"` and a quoted path ending in git; the vocabularies are named constants with `// contract: R-2351`. The leading pipefail exemption, PowerShell pipefail as inactive, quoted heredoc bodies and the reason text are unchanged. Rows R-2350 to R-2357 sit in FEAT-010 after R-984; R-982 is retired, superseded by R-2350 to R-2354; R-1064 is reworded. Every test case whose pipe must stay live moved from `;` or a newline to `&&`, and the install check's sealed PowerShell sample is now `npm test | Select-Object -Last 5 && git commit -m x`. install-check.test.mjs picks hook calls by the hook script's file name, so it passes from a folder whose path holds a hook name. Both README guard lines and the setup README's hooks-table sentence state the read-status rule. CAP-03 moves from 171 to 179 rows and FEAT-010 from 76 to 84. pipe-guard.test.mjs reads 198 PASS, against 84 on main.

**Evidence.** CI run 39508818938 on draft pull request #149 at e45d4656 (build 5, the seat's pairs record and a merge of main 7aadbc99) reads 0 failing on all three legs: macOS 196 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP of 198 files (8,157 checks pass, 36 skip); Ubuntu 195 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP (8,096 pass, 56 skip); Windows 180 PASS, 0 FAIL, 18 SKIP (7,086 pass, 114 skip). On Windows hooks-win32-exec passes 31, including R-1064's three checks, and the span oracle ran pwsh and Windows PowerShell (38 pass). The install check passes on macOS and Windows. Earlier runs on builds 1 to 4 were cancelled as superseded. The three final survivors are declared: K1 (a backslash-CRLF outside quotes, where real bash behaves like the wrong form), K8 (no honest test can tell it apart) and C1 (the install check's PowerShell sample runs only on Windows). Four independent checks ran, one per build from 1 to 4 (details under seat items). ## 2026-10-20 — the knowledge build replaces a damaged index with one rebuilt from the sources and names the damage, status names it with the repair, and a damaged index stays unchanged while the sources file does not parse

Spend served the current priority's hook line: the knowledge build that both seats' prompt hooks start in the background, working the same way on macOS and Windows. The plan probed main 72abe19a in a temp copy (macOS). An index.db of random bytes threw SQLite code 26 at the open, and a half-truncated one threw 11 there, each with a stack and exit 1. With the files table's root page overwritten, the build threw 11 at its files query. With the docs table's root page overwritten, the build resolved, because it reads only the files table, and moved the index age, so the hooks stopped starting builds for an hour while every query threw 11. A docs or files table of another shape threw code 1. `status` printed a stack over random bytes and healthy counts over the docs-page fixture. The adversary's probe on a 25 MB index overwrote whole pages at 10 to 99% of the file: the no-op build resolved every time, and at 90 to 99%, 1 to 5 of 20 pulls failed. The owner's real pull.log held 978 lines and no query-failed, so the hardening is speculative but cheap. The seat's re-check on the knowledge-sources-unparseable land tip added a damaged index under an unparseable sources.json: random bytes and half truncation exited 1 with a stack for `build` and `build --rebuild`, and the docs-page fixture had index.db rewritten.

**The change.** `packages/nana-knowledge/lib/db.ts` adds `DAMAGE_CODES` (SQLite primary codes 1, 11 and 26; contract: R-2400, R-2401), `IndexDamageError`, `indexDamage(err)` and `checkIndex(db)`, which runs `PRAGMA quick_check(1)` and throws "database disk image is malformed: <first finding>" on anything but "ok"; openDb closes its handle when its setup throws. `lib/build.ts` reads sources.json once, inside the build lock's `try`. With good sources, buildLocked runs checkIndex after every open and closes its handle in a `finally`; build() catches once, and damage on a build that was not already a rebuild runs `buildLocked({ rebuild: true })` and sets `recovered`. Under a sources problem with an index present, a read-only handle runs checkIndex first: a damaged index returns stats with `keptDamage` and nothing is written; a healthy one is reopened read-write without the schema step and finishes as main does (rows kept, `built_at` refreshed, the checkpoint run, shown/ pruned). With no index, it creates an empty one, as main does. Nothing is checked or deleted before the lock. `bin/nana-knowledge.ts` prints `  index was damaged (<reason>) — rebuilt from the sources` on a recovery, or `  index was damaged (<reason>) — not rebuilt while sources.json has a problem; repair it, then run nana-knowledge build` and the sources marker, exit 0, on a keep; a recovery gives MISSING and UNREADABLE roots the rebuild wording. status prints `index <db> is damaged (<reason>) — repair: nana-knowledge build --rebuild` and exits 0. ## 2026-10-20 — the Claude Code seat's shared-memory hook keeps its session-start output under Claude Code's hook output cap, cutting the longest descriptions first and naming what it cut

## 2026-10-20 — on Windows, review-ledger run refuses a .cmd or .bat reviewer path that names no file in the reviewed tree, and names the path it looked for

Spend served the current priority's Windows line: nana working in terminal mode for both seats on macOS and Windows, installation and every hook included; the review tools are the maintainer-tools part of the Windows fixes. review-ledger-run-win-launch's final review left a carried residual: on win32 the resolver took a `.cmd` or `.bat` path as given. Off win32 nothing changes, because the resolver reads cwd only there. R-2252's fixture gains the `.bat` it launches, and the pack README's Windows paragraph gains one sentence: a relative path is read from the reviewed tree, and a `.cmd` or `.bat` path that names no file there is refused with the cannot-start line before cmd.exe starts. The build's purge then read every row's root as gone from sources.json and deleted the row. The plan probed main 72abe19a in a temp copy with a temp home: after a good build, sources.json re-saved six ways (a UTF-8 mark, UTF-16LE with a mark, a `C:\` path, a trailing comma, an empty file, a folder in its place) each gave `removed 1`, exit 0, and then `(no hits)`. `build --rebuild` on the `C:\` file also left `(no hits)`, and `status` printed only `sources <file>`. ## 2026-10-20 — in pi, a plain rm or rm -f whose target lies outside the working folder and every temp folder asks first and names that target

Spend served the current priority's hook line: the pi seat's gate, here its rm check, working the same way on macOS and Windows. It carries out the owner's 2026-10-20 morning ruling that a plain rm or rm -f outside the working folder must ask first. On main, pi's bash and PowerShell tools ran a non-recursive delete of a target outside the working folder unasked; only recursive or `--force` forms asked there. The plan probed main 72abe19a headless in a temp clone, twice: 21 outside spellings ran unasked (14 bash, 7 PowerShell), and so did `rm -i`, `rm -d` and `rm --verbose`. A headless ask is a block, because pi-worker and pi-review run pi in print mode. So the plan measured the cost first: a prototype replay of 376 recorded rm-shaped pi calls gave 1 new ask with a temp-folder pass and 73 reviewer blocks without one.

**The change.** `lib/gate-shell.ts` exports `commandIndex`, `base` and `PS_REMOVE`, with no behaviour change. New `packages/nana-pack/lib/gate-rm-outside.ts` exports `rmOutsideTargets(segments, cwd, tool, { home, tempRoots, segmentable })`, a Map from segment to the full path of its first outside target. It reads bash `rm` and PowerShell `Remove-Item` and its aliases in command position (behind `command`, `/bin/rm`, `\rm` and the other wrappers `commandIndex` skips), every target word, the words after `--`, `-Path` and `-LiteralPath` values, and a leading `~`, `$HOME` or `${HOME}` (PowerShell also `$env:USERPROFILE` and `$env:HOME`). It drops redirection operands. A target led by another variable, a backtick or `~user` is not judged; a glob or variable in a later part is judged as a child of the literal folder before it. A `cd`, `pushd` or PowerShell location command moves where relative targets are judged; in a command the gate cannot split, it adds a folder instead. A target's place is the real path of its parent plus its last name, and outside means not strictly inside the real working folder or any real temp root, by the shared `within(parent, child)` of `lib/gate-temp-roots.ts`. The module never throws: an internal failure counts the segment as outside. `commandHit` in `extensions/nana-gate.ts` runs it after the floor loop and the in-folder exemption, over the exec segments and, for a command it cannot split, over the detection segments. A hit segment with no danger yet gets the non-floor reason `rm outside the working folder: <path>`; allow patterns and the later checks run after it, unchanged. One helper in `nana-gate.ts`, `gateTempRoots()`, gives both the rm check and the lane write guard the shared temp roots plus `/tmp`, resolved, on macOS and Linux; `laneWriteHit` keeps its behaviour. Rows R-2330 to R-2338 sit in FEAT-010 after R-2243, with nine checks in `packages/nana-pack/tests/gate-rm-outside.test.mjs`; R-2338's check prints a real SKIP on Windows. The pack README gains the rule's gate bullet and drops the in-folder bullet's "separate lane" sentence. CAP-03 moves from 157 to 166 rows and FEAT-010 from 67 to 76.

**Evidence.** CI on draft pull request #140: run 39457512319 on build 1 (3d8e2d22) was cancelled as superseded. Run 39460770013 runs at 490bb78b, build 2 plus the seat's pairs record. Its macOS, Ubuntu and Windows legs were still running when the reviews started; the seat reads the Windows leg before the land, as the plan says. The seat's wrong-code pairs on macOS (Node 22.22.2, one shard): on build 1, 27 of 30 red (`seat-mutate-output-3d8e2d22.txt`). **Plan and build.** The seat's plan went to one adversary, which amended it after probing a temp clone of 72abe19a. A cd inside a subshell could miss a delete (`(cd sub/deep && true); rm ../../x`), so in a command the gate cannot split a cd now adds a folder instead of replacing one. **Known limits.** A target led by another variable, a command substitution or `~user`, or a relative target after an unreadable cd, is not judged. A session started in home or a filesystem root sees nothing under it as outside. Temp folders are shared, so a plain rm of another session's file there runs unasked; on macOS and Linux `/tmp` counts even with home inside it (read from the code, not run). A glob or variable in a folder part is judged by the literal folder before it, and `..` after a linked folder is judged lexically. In a command the gate can split, a cd applies to the rest of the line even when it fails or sits in a pipeline. Only rm in command position is judged; `unlink`, bash `rmdir`, `mv` and a truncating redirect are not, and the recursive and forced reasons still name no path. Heredoc lines that look like rm are judged. Git Bash `/tmp` and `/c/` paths ask. PowerShell colon-bound parameters, pipeline input, filter and include scope and backtick escapes are not read. The pairs and the independent check ran on macOS only.

## 2026-10-20 — on Windows, a kill of install or of its relay ends an npm-installed pi, because install, its dry run and doctor start it through its Node entry instead of Command Prompt

Spend served the current priority's Windows line: nana working in terminal mode for both seats on macOS and Windows, installation and every hook included; install's pi launch is part of the Windows install shape. On main 72abe19a, install, its dry run and doctor ran every located `.cmd` pi through ComSpec (`cmd.exe /d /v:off /s /c`), under the pi launch relay that holds the launch's time limit. The seat's Windows probe (run 39437686060, a scratch windows-latest job) showed what a kill did on that route: a kill of install ended the relay and cmd.exe within 65 ms, while pi and its child were still alive 5 s later; a kill of the relay alone left them alive too. The plan's reading of libuv's Windows process code explains it: Node puts each non-detached child into a kill-on-close job that allows silent breakaway and adds the spawning process to that job, so the relay's job nests inside install's; cmd.exe is not a Node process, so the pi it starts joins no job (read in the code, then matched by the probe). HANDOFF said pi then ran until its limit and the relay ended it. The plan adversary showed, and the probe confirmed, that the relay dies with install, so such a pi ran with no limit. The adversary also found a second red case: with an npm pi and a checkout path holding `%` and `!`, install read `pi install refused: refused character %`.

**The change.** New `packages/nana-setup/lib/pi-invocation.mjs` exports `piInvocation(pi, args, { win32, env, cwd, exists, isFile, readText })`. Off win32 it starts pi by name, as main does. On win32 it calls pi-watchdog's `piLaunch` (R-1125, imported, not moved, since review-launch imports it from there); when pi's npm package resolves, the launch is `<running node> <entry> <args>` with no ComSpec and no verbatim-arguments flag. Any piLaunch refusal falls back to main's route through `winCommand`, with ComSpec read in any key case; the fallback never surfaces piLaunch's reason. `stepPiRegister` (`lib/steps.mjs`) and doctor's pi block (`lib/doctor.mjs`) both call it and take `isFile` and `readText` beside `exists`, so doctor's duplicate ComSpec block goes. The relay files do not change: a pi the relay starts itself joins the relay's job, and pi's own Node children join pi's, all nested in install's (read in libuv; the probe and the two Windows checks then saw it). Rows R-2300 to R-2303 sit in FEAT-013 SUB-013 after R-2133: R-2300 (a kill of install alone ends an npm pi launch on Windows), R-2301 (install, the dry run and doctor start an npm pi.cmd's entry with the running Node, the arguments, limit and environment unchanged, without ComSpec), R-2302 (a pi.cmd with no resolvable npm package still runs through ComSpec) and R-2303 (a kill of the relay alone ends that pi and its child). R-1034, R-1035 and R-1690 are reworded to cover only the ComSpec route; their tests stay green unchanged, because no fixture they use has pi's npm package beside its shim. All four checks are in `packages/nana-setup/tests/pi-launch-limits.test.mjs`; R-2300 and R-2303 use a new npm fixture (a `pi.cmd` running `process.execPath` on the package's `cli.js`) and run only on Windows. The setup README's Windows lookup paragraph says an npm `pi.cmd` starts its package's Node entry and any other `.cmd` or `.bat` runs through ComSpec; Idempotence says an npm pi also ends when install is killed on Windows; Known limits gains the plan's list. CAP-04 moves from 500 to 504 rows, FEAT-013 from 189 to 193 and SUB-013 from 47 to 51.

**Evidence.** CI run 39441915006 on draft pull request #139 at c0856720 (build 1; GitHub's merge commit merges it into its own base 72abe19a): macOS 188 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP of 190 files (7,964 checks pass); Ubuntu 187 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP (7,903); Windows 172 PASS, 0 FAIL, 18 SKIP (6,891 pass, 112 skip), its skips main's declared 18; install-check passes on macOS and Windows. On native Windows pi-launch-limits passes 12 with 5 skips and prints PASS for R-2300 and R-2303, then still `req-candidate`, as well as R-2301 and R-2302. The Windows install check ran a real npm pi 1.0.2 and printed PASS for install, both pi package lists and doctor, the plan's seat check before land; it prints no route, so the direct route there is inferred from the layout. On macOS and Ubuntu pi-launch-limits reads 15 pass, 2 skip. None of main's known failures showed. Build 2 changes only the two markers, their two rows and one README sentence, so CI has not run on it. The seat's wrong-code pairs on c0856720 (macOS, Node 22.22.2, one shard): 12 of 12 red, 0 survived (`seat-mutate-output-c0856720.txt`). **Plan and build.** The seat wrote the plan with a probe-first step: four branches, chosen by the probe's last line, decided the build. The plan went to one adversary, which amended it. It found in libuv that the spawning process joins its own job, so the relay's job nests in install's, and that HANDOFF's "until its limit" line was very likely wrong. ## 2026-10-20 — doctor gives the pi-review PATH row to install when the bin folder is already on PATH and only the launcher is missing

Spend served the current priority's installation line: nana working in terminal mode for both seats on macOS and Windows, installation and every hook included. Doctor is the ✓/✗ instrument for a machine, and since doctor-fix-line (2026-10-19) its last line names install only for the ✗ rows install's dry run would repair. On main 72abe19a, the `PATH resolves pi-review` row on the real home, when ✗, always gave the add-to-PATH fix (`add <bin> to PATH — zsh: echo …` on macOS and Linux, `add <bin> to the user Path in Environment Variables…` on Windows) and carried no install label, so the last line listed it by hand. That held when the bin folder was already a PATH entry and only the launcher was missing, a case install repairs by recreating the launcher. The plan adversary's probe on 72abe19a (temp clone, temp HOME, macOS) printed `3 missing — fix by hand as each ✗ line says: PATH resolves pi-review; then run: nana-setup install for the other 2`, and a forced win32 run listed the row by hand among 5. HANDOFF carried it from doctor-fix-line.

**The change.** `packages/nana-setup/lib/doctor.mjs`, the PATH section's two branches. Doctor finds `binAt`, the first PATH entry equal to the bin folder: on win32 it splits on `;` with findOnPath's trim and quote strip and compares `path.win32.resolve` on both sides, lowercased; on POSIX it splits on `path.delimiter` and compares `path.resolve`. `installFixes` holds when the row is wrong, `binAt >= 0`, and no pi-review resolves from the entries before `binAt` (POSIX `firstOnPath` over that slice; win32 `findOnPath` with an env of only PATH and PATHEXT, because a spread of `process.env` would let Windows' own `Path` key outrank the injected PATH). When it holds, the row's detail reads `<found | not found>; <bin> is on PATH — run \`nana-setup install\` to recreate the launcher`, and the row carries installLabel `PATH pi-review`. Install's existing dry-run mapping in `nana-setup.mjs` then decides the last line, so a launcher that install would leave unchanged keeps the row by hand. Every other case keeps main's detail and no label. `nana-setup.mjs`, `steps.mjs` and `fsops.mjs` are unchanged. The setup README's dry-run paragraph now says `PATH resolves pi-review` goes to install when the bin folder is already on PATH and no earlier PATH entry holds a pi-review, and that doctor otherwise lists it by hand. Rows R-2320 to R-2325 sit in FEAT-015 after R-1997, with their checks in `packages/nana-setup/tests/doctor-fix-line.test.mjs`. The checks run doctor with no --home (the real-home branch) on a controlled PATH through a new `runOnPath`, which spawns the CLI directly. R-1993's by-hand regex moves into a shared `byHandOf`, and `toInstall` accepts only the plain run-install form or the then-run form. R-2323 runs forced win32 on every host; the rest run natively on all three. CAP-04 moves from 500 to 506 rows and FEAT-015 from 138 to 144.

On native Windows doctor-fix-line passes 15, all six new checks among them. So the win32 earlier-entry lookup ran natively, which no Mac probe can do; that was the plan's claim most likely wrong, and it held. None of main's known failures showed. The first CI run, 39439715494 on build 1 452cd604, failed the requirements trace: each new check's `// req:` marker sat above a `check(` call whose title was on the next line. The seat's wrong-code pairs on 452cd604 (macOS, Node 22.22.2, one shard): 12 of 12 red, 0 survived (`seat-mutate-output-452cd604.txt`). ## 2026-10-20 — on Windows, review-ledger run starts an npm-installed claude or codex reviewer, and on every platform a command it cannot start ends with one named line

Spend served the current priority's Windows line: nana working in terminal mode for both seats on macOS and Windows, installation and every hook included; the review tools are the maintainer-tools part of the Windows fixes. A seat hands a hand-run reviewer, such as `claude -p`, to `review-ledger run`, which reserves the round, runs the command and records its verdict. Before this lane, `review-ledger.mjs` took pi's npm launch only for a first word of exactly `pi` (review-ledger-run-reviewer, 2026-10-19) and started every other word by name. libuv's Windows lookup tries only .com and .exe, so an npm `claude.cmd` ended `no verdict (exit ENOENT…)` (inferred from libuv and the pack README). The spawn sat inside a `new Promise` executor, so a synchronous throw became a top-level rejection. The plan's probes on main a112fd30 (temp clone, temp HOME, macOS): `run … -- ""` printed the admission note, then a raw `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]` stack; it exited 1, kept the reservation file and wrote no --out. `run … -- nana-absent-reviewer-xyz` printed `no verdict (exit ENOENT; 0 chars)` and left an empty --out. A refused pi launch wrote nothing to --out, which two HANDOFF residuals from review-ledger-run-reviewer recorded.

**The change.** New `packages/nana-pack/bin/review-launch.mjs` exports `reviewLaunch(child, opts)`, pure under injection (platform, env, cwd, file probes, execPath). Off win32 it keeps today's start: an exact `pi` through `piLaunch`, anything else by name. On win32, a bare pi name in any letter case, alone or with .com, .exe, .bat or .cmd, takes `piLaunch`, whose refusal reads `pi launch refused: <reason>`. A word holding `\`, `/` or `:` is a path taken as given; a .cmd or .bat path goes through `winCommand`'s `cmd.exe /d /v:off /s /c` line and anything else starts directly. Any other bare word goes through `findOnPath` (PATH-folder order, then PATHEXT order): a found .exe or .com starts directly, a .cmd or .bat goes through ComSpec (read in any key case), another extension is refused, named, and no match is refused `not on PATH`. `review-ledger.mjs` calls it where it called `piLaunch`. A refusal now runs after admission: `cannotStart` releases the reservation, writes `cannot start <word>: <reason>` to --out as a best effort (an empty word prints as `""`) and dies with that line. The spawn moved out of the Promise into a try with `{...launch.options, cwd, stdio, env}`. A throw stops the heartbeat and calls `cannotStart(e.code ?? e.message)`, and so does the spawn's `error` event (the adversary's amendment), since review-ledger never kills or signals its child. `win-command.mjs` and `pi-watchdog.mjs` are unchanged, and pi-review does not use the resolver. The R-1723 Windows check gains one condition, --out starting `cannot start pi: pi launch refused:`, and its marker reads `req: R-1723 R-2250`. The pack README's run paragraph names the cannot-start line. A new Windows note says a .cmd reviewer starts through cmd.exe, lists what cmd.exe cannot carry, and gives a Command Prompt example that feeds the brief on stdin and writes --out under a fresh %TEMP% folder. The Windows paragraph's last sentence says how review-ledger run routes each spelling. Rows R-2250 to R-2255 sit in FEAT-007 SUB-008 after R-1723, and the new `review-launch.test.mjs` holds all six. ## 2026-10-20 — nana's readers of nana-pack.json read the file saved as UTF-16 with its byte-order mark, as Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes it

Spend served the current priority's Windows line: nana working in terminal mode for both seats on macOS and Windows, installation and every hook included. Windows PowerShell 5.1's `>` and `Out-File` write UTF-16LE with a byte-order mark by default. Every nana reader of nana-pack.json decoded its bytes as UTF-8, so such a file never parsed; bom-pack-config (2026-10-19) carried that as a residual. The plan's probes on main, in a throwaway clone under a temp home: pi's gate stopped every gated tool, `ls` included, with "gate block is malformed … invalid JSON"; the Claude Code objective producer printed the objective plus "NANA-PACK CONFIG UNPARSEABLE" for `objective.enabled: false`, so the owner could not turn the objective off; `nana-roster --json` and `set` refused with "invalid JSON"; doctor read the pi nana-pack.json row ✗, the default projectFile and the objective file ✗; `project --check` lost the post-edit commands; the adoption settings fell back to the default journal and OBJECTIVE.md.

**The change.** `packages/nana-pack/lib/json-text.mjs` gains `parseJsonBytes`. A buffer that starts FF FE decodes whole, mark included, as UTF-16LE; one that starts FE FF is copied, `swap16`'d and decoded the same way; an odd byte count after either mark throws a SyntaxError before any swap; anything else decodes as UTF-8, as before. The text then goes through `parseJsonText`, which removes exactly one U+FEFF, so R-1586's two-mark rule holds in every encoding. The two marks are contract constants. Decoding and parsing happen in one call, so a bad UTF-16 file lands in each reader's existing catch with its existing fallback and message. Seven readers switch to it: `config.ts` `readConfigFile` (the pi gate and objective extensions and the Claude Code objective producer), `adoption.mjs` `adoptionSettings` (both adoption seats), `nana-roster.mjs` `readRosterFile` and `resolveRoster` (nana-roster, the roster notice, pi-worker and pi-review), `roster-set.mjs`, `doctor.mjs` `piPackConfigState`, `steps.mjs` `readPiPackConfig` (doctor and install's objective seed) and `project.mjs`'s `.pi/nana-pack.json` parse. The pi settings.json readers keep `parseJsonText`. No file that parses on main reads differently, since FE and FF never occur in UTF-8. `nana-roster set` re-serializes the file, so it writes UTF-8, and `.bak` keeps the original bytes. The pack README gains a Config encodings bullet, names marked UTF-16 in the roster's byte-order-mark sentence and says `set` rewrites the file as UTF-8. Rows R-2230 to R-2237 sit in FEAT-015 after R-1586, one per reader path plus the unparseable shapes (R-2236) and the Windows PowerShell proof (R-2237). CAP-04 moves from 489 to 497 rows and FEAT-015 from 128 to 136.

**Evidence.** CI run 39418143889 on draft pull request #128 at 2d2ba429 (build 2 plus the seat's merge of main 0305bc8d): macOS 185 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP of 187 files (7,943 checks pass); Ubuntu 184 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP (7,882); Windows 170 PASS, 0 FAIL, 17 SKIP (6,874 pass, 111 skip), its skips main's declared ones; install-check passes on macOS and Windows. On native Windows pack-config-utf16 passes 5 of 5, including R-2237: a nana-pack.json written by Windows PowerShell's `Out-File` and by its `>` turns the objective off. That was the plan's claim most likely wrong, and it held; build 1's run 39414266878 at 961f76d1 passed it first. None of main's known failures showed. The seat's wrong-code pairs: 19 of 19 red, 0 survived, each exactly on its named titles, on 961f76d1, on build 2 (58e2da48) and on the merged tip 69f0a82e (records `seat-mutate-output-961f76d1.txt`, `-58e2da48.txt` and `-69f0a82e.txt`). Each reader reverted to main's decode turns its own row red, and twelve wrong decoders (odd count allowed, marks sliced, TextDecoder defaults, every mark stripped, no BE swap, no BE branch, NUL sniffing, the UTF-8 mark kept, the marks swapped) turn R-2236, R-2230 or the existing UTF-8 byte-order-mark checks red. The independent check on 961f76d1 HOLDS over nine probes with no MUST. The trace reads 1,619 rows, 0 off form; map:check reads 353 modules, 0 problems; readme:check reads 723 claims, 0 problems; requirements-moved lists R-2230 to R-2237 new and implemented in FEAT-015. The seat's record is `docs/reviews/pack-config-utf16-2026-10-20/seat-verify-6cc66daf.md`, with the Windows log and the independent check beside it.

**Plan and build.** The seat's plan went to one adversary, which amended it. R-2232 narrowed from "treat it exactly as" to byte-identical `--json` output and a byte-identical file from `set`, which it probed. R-2236's test gained the BE shapes, six in all. Two likely builder mistakes joined the wrong-code list, slicing the mark bytes and TextDecoder's default ignoreBOM, both of which strip two marks. Every child process in the tests sets HOME, USERPROFILE and PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to the temp home, and the `set` child drops PI_SESSION_ID, so the test neither fails under pi-worker nor rewrites a real file. ## 2026-10-20 — on macOS and Linux, install converges every link and the knowledge hook an earlier install wrote through another spelling of the checkout, and uninstall removes that entry

Spend served the current priority's installation line: nana working in terminal mode for both seats on macOS and Windows, installation and every hook included. The change is macOS and Linux only; Windows output is unchanged. setup-checkout-spelling left two gaps in its one-time convergence of a home an earlier install wrote through another spelling of the checkout, both HANDOFF residuals. The plan's probes on a temp clone of main aa5f25cd (macOS, temp homes), with every link text and hook command rewritten to a letter-case or a linked spelling of the checkout: install relinked 16 links, but spec, py-lint, py-review and py-test printed "unchanged" and kept the old text, because `linkSkill`'s foreign-link branch returned UNCHANGED whenever the real paths matched. Through the linked spelling, install called the knowledge hook "already wired" and kept the link spelling; the case spelling was already rewritten, since the healthy check's JS realpath keeps a typed case. And uninstall printed "settings hook variant skipped left" and left the knowledge entry through both spellings, because `removeInstallerHooks` removed only exact objects. A linked spelling arises when a checkout moves and leaves a link at its old path; install never writes one itself.

**The change.** In `packages/nana-setup/lib/steps.mjs`, `linkSkill` enters the foreign-link branch only when the link's text, resolved against its folder, differs from the source. There it compares `realPath(…, { mustExist: true })` of link and source: a dangling link or another real path stays the PROBLEM "foreign link … — left untouched", and a match falls through to the ordinary relink ("would relink (was …)" on a dry run). `lib/settings.mjs` gains one private predicate, `respelledKnowledgeEntry`: the entry has no `args`, both commands name an installer knowledge target, the commands differ, every other key equals the wanted entry, and both targets are one file under the native lookup, a throw reading false. On win32 the wanted entry has `args`, so the predicate is false there by construction. `removeInstallerHooks` removes an exact or a respelled entry, and `mergeRepoHooks` also replaces a healthy "posix"-form entry whose command differs and whose target is the same file; the win32 branch is unchanged. The healthy check keeps `fs.realpathSync`, now with a comment saying why. `lib/uninstall.mjs`'s `settingsVariants` reads the settings after removal. `scripts/test.mjs` declares the new file's skip on win32, since an all-skip file is a runner failure. The setup README rewrites the earlier-spelling bullet and the uninstall sentence and adds a tests-table row. Rows R-2200 and R-2201 sit in FEAT-013 SUB-012 after R-665, R-2202 in SUB-013 after R-1984, and R-2203 and R-2204 in FEAT-018 after R-1985. CAP-04 moves from 474 to 479 rows, FEAT-013 from 180 to 183 (SUB-012 39 to 41, SUB-013 45 to 46) and FEAT-018 from 22 to 24. The new `checkout-converge.test.mjs` runs each check through the link spelling on every POSIX host and the case spelling where it exists. Its earlier-home fixture fails when it rewrites no link or no knowledge entry.

**Evidence.** CI run 39409313594 on draft pull request #125 at 29b83bf4 (GitHub's merge commit 3f2cfc8a merges 29b83bf4 into its own ancestor c7f582ad, so the tree tested is 29b83bf4's): macOS 179 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP of 181 files (7,919 checks pass); Ubuntu 178 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP (7,858); Windows 163 PASS, 0 FAIL, 18 SKIP (6,845 pass, 110 skip); install-check passes on macOS and Windows. ## 2026-10-20 — in pi, a plain rm in or of a bare git repository asks again

That lane's exemption lets a plain recursive or forced rm of literal targets inside the working folder run unasked, and it spots a git repository only by a `.git` entry directly under a target. A bare repository has no `.git` entry. The plan's probe on main 6f0098a8's module: with bare repositories under the cwd, `rm -rf vault`, `vault/objects`, `vault/refs/heads` and `repos/mirror.git/objects` ran unasked headless with 0 dialogs; from a `git clone --bare` folder and the folders inside it, `rm -rf objects`, `refs`, `heads`, `topic` and `wt` did too. ## 2026-10-20 — doctor, the session-start line, uninstall's preview and the land and review tools work where Node's native path lookup fails

Spend served the current priority's installation-and-hooks line on Windows ("installation and every hook included"): it closes setup-checkout-spelling's final-review finding. That lane moved nana-setup's compares against the checkout to `realPath(x, { mustExist: true })`, which rethrew any native error other than a missing file. Node's `realpathSync.native` fails on some Windows virtual volumes where `fs.realpathSync` works; vite's `optimizeSafeRealPathSync` documents EISDIR from ImDisk virtual and RAM disks and switches lookups there. The plan's probes on a clone of main 773de493, macOS, with the native lookup patched to throw: realPath under mustExist threw EISDIR, EIO, EPERM and UNKNOWN; doctor flipped 21 of 48 POSIX rows and 6 of 44 forced-win32 rows from ✓ to ✗; the stale-copy producer printed `INSTALL STALE` on both forms; `uninstall --dry-run` exited 1 with `✗ uninstall preflight problem EISDIR: injected native failure`. The independent check added three more on its base clone aa5f25cd: review-round's key threw EISDIR, nana-land refused a land with the injected error, and install exited 1 on a home holding a legacy `context-size-check.sh` link.

**The change.** One change, in `realPath`'s catch in `packages/nana-pack/lib/real-path.mjs`: on a native error other than ENOENT/ENOTDIR it tries `fs.realpathSync(abs)` first, with or without `mustExist`; only when that also throws does it rethrow the native error under `mustExist`, or return `abs` without it. ## 2026-10-20 — only one waiter at a time takes over a dead shard's mutation-runner lock

Spend served the current priority's Windows line through the seat's own tools. The mutation runner judges the seat's wrong-code pairs, and HANDOFF recorded that its contention check had never taken over a dead holder's lock on Windows. The lane also restores R-1776, an implemented no-overlap row known broken in the single-kill takeover case. `withWorktreeOperationLock` in `packages/nana-pack/lib/mutation-runner.mjs` removed a dead owner's lock by reading it, comparing it and unlinking it (`removeWorktreeLockIfOwned`). Waiter B read dead content X and stalled just before its unlink; A removed X, published its own lock and entered; B then unlinked A's fresh lock, published its own and entered too. The mutation-runner-lock-overlap planner found it. This lane's planner probed a temp copy of main 773de493: two child waiters, with B paused in the existing `unlinkSync` seam, recorded `B found A` for a dead pid and for an old unreadable lock, 3 runs of 3. Pausing B after its first read stayed green, because the removal re-read before it unlinked. The race needs a shard killed while it holds the lock plus two live waiters; git then fails loudly and the shard is refused, so a pair goes missing rather than a verdict going wrong.

**The change.** `lib/mutation-runner-config.mjs` adds `WORKTREE_LOCK_BREAKER_SUFFIX = ".break"`, `chosen` and naming R-2170, listed in `@outputs`, not sealed and not overridable (precedent `LOCK_SUFFIX`). `lib/mutation-runner.mjs` extracts two helpers that the lock and the breaker share: `judgeWorktreeLock` (read, parse, pid alive, unreadable age) and `releaseWorktreeLock` (R-1960's bounded release loop). A waiter that judges the lock dead publishes `<lock>.break` with `publishWorktreeLock`, the lock's own temp-plus-link step, so one waiter at a time holds it. Holding it, the waiter judges the lock again and removes it, compare-then-remove, only if it is still dead with the same content; a `finally` releases the breaker before any wait or throw, and the waiter then waits on a transient result or retries at once. A live breaker holder makes the others wait through `waitOrFail`. A dead or old unreadable breaker is removed by compare-then-remove, and the waiter retries at once. Every breaker file operation goes through the injected `io`. R-1775 and R-1777 to R-1779 and R-1960 keep their values and behaviour. The module's `@effects` names the breaker files, and the pack README's Limits paragraph gains two sentences: only one waiter at a time removes a dead shard's lock, and a waiter killed while removing one, plus a later dead shard, can still let two in. The new `packages/nana-pack/tests/mutation-runner-takeover.test.mjs` pins R-2170 (two child waiters, B paused after its read or before its removal, each with a dead pid and an old unreadable lock; A must signal before B's release), R-2171 (a child that kills itself at its first unlink of the lock; an in-process waiter then enters before the wait limit on a fake clock) and R-2172 (a per-call sweep: one EPERM, EACCES or EBUSY at each read, stat, link or unlink of a fault-free takeover, then a plain takeover of the next dead lock). The rows sit in FEAT-031 after R-1960; FEAT-031 moves from 92 to 95 rows and CAP-07 from 307 to 310. The code map and the tree are regenerated.

**Evidence.** CI run 39406441608 on draft pull request #122 at e943d4de (GitHub's merge commit 6a6d6cdc merges e943d4de into its own ancestor aa5f25cd, so the tree tested is e943d4de's): macOS 178 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP of 180 files (7,911 checks pass); Ubuntu 177 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP (7,850); Windows 163 PASS, 0 FAIL, 17 SKIP (6,847 pass, 107 skip), its skips main's declared ones; install-check passes on macOS and Windows. None of main's known failures showed. The new file reads 3 pass on macOS (1.4 s), Ubuntu (0.5 s) and Windows (1.3 s), and on Windows R-2170, R-2171 and R-2172 each print PASS by title. So the plan's known limit that Windows behaviour stays inferred until the seat reads the Windows leg is closed. mutation-runner.test.mjs reads 39 pass on macOS (57.1 s) and Ubuntu (20.9 s) and `37 pass, 3 skip  86.3s` on Windows, as on main, with the contention check, the transient lock error check and R-1960 printing PASS there. The builder showed R-2170 red before the change, `B found A` for both before-removal dead-lock kinds. Per its report, W1 (today's code), W2 (no re-check under the breaker) and W3 (a breaker written by plain overwrite) each turn R-2170 red; W4 (a dead breaker never removed) turns R-2171 red; W5 to W8 (the breaker kept after a transient lock removal error, a transient breaker release given up, the breaker never released, the breaker kept after a transient re-read error) each turn R-2172 red. The new file ran green three times on macOS (0.99 s, 0.98 s, 0.95 s). The seat re-ran none. The plan's prototype passed R-2170 in 5 runs of 5 and the sweep's 63 cases in 0.4 s; today's code passed R-2171 and the sweep's 45 cases. No seat pairs and no independent check: an ordinary lane. `requirements-moved --base main` lists R-2170, R-2171 and R-2172 as new (implemented) in FEAT-031. The trace reads 1,577 rows, 0 off form; map:check reads 343 modules, 0 problems. The seat's record is `docs/reviews/mutation-runner-takeover-race-2026-10-20/seat-verify-e943d4de.md`, with the Windows log beside it.

**Plan and build.** The seat's plan went to one adversary, which amended it. R-2172 became a per-call fault sweep, because the first plan's first-call-per-path faults missed W8: the re-read under the breaker never got the first-call fault. R-2171 was narrowed to "just before it removes", the only kill point the test reaches. R-2170's pass now needs A's signal before B's release, so a slow Windows runner cannot pass today's code by never reaching the schedule. Fake clocks start at `Date.now()`, since a clock at 0 judged an old unreadable lock fresh. The adversary also corrected a known-limits claim: R-1778's check already takes over a dead-pid lock and an old unreadable lock in-process on every leg, Windows included. Claude Opus 5.5 (the final reviewer) reviews it through review-ledger.

**Known limits.** A dead breaker is still removed by compare-then-remove, so a waiter killed while holding the breaker, a second dead lock and two live waiters with a stall can bring the race back; this is reasoned, not probed, and no check covers it. A live but stalled breaker holder makes the others wait, and their wait-limit line may name the dead lock's pid rather than the breaker holder's. Breaker release reuses the 300000 ms release limit, so on a Windows path that stays delete-pending a waiter can outlast the 30000 ms acquisition limit, the same trade as R-1960. The user gain is small: today the race fails loudly as a missing pair.

## 2026-10-20 — on macOS and Linux, killing install ends its pi launch too, and pi output up to 1 MiB a stream reads as pi's own result again

Spend served the current priority's installation line: nana working in terminal mode for both seats on macOS and Windows, installation included. pi-probe-timeout put a relay behind every pi launch of install, its dry run and doctor, and its plan, independent check and review left five known bugs on it. This lane fixes three. First, the relay ran in install's process group while pi ran in its own session, so a supervisor's SIGKILL of install's group (or `timeout -s KILL`) ended install and the relay but not pi. In the plan's probe on a hung fake pi that ignores SIGINT, sh, the fake pi and its child were all alive at the 2.2 s bound, and nothing would ever end them. A SIGKILL of install alone left the orphaned relay waiting out the launch's limit (12 s in the probe). Second, the relay wrote pi's stdout and stderr as one JSON line, which the outer spawnSync capped at its default 1 MiB, so a `pi install` that wrote just under 1 MiB of control characters to each stream read `failed: spawnSync <node> ENOBUFS` on exit 0 and on exit 1. Third, on Windows the launch test file printed PASS after each skipped check, so its summary counted nine passes where seven checks ran.

**The change.** In `packages/nana-setup/lib/bounded-spawn.mjs`, the outer spawnSync that starts the relay passes `detached: true` on POSIX only, so the relay leads its own session and a kill of install's group misses it; the win32 options are unchanged. The launch spec gains `parentPid: process.pid`, and the outer call takes `maxBuffer: RELAY_RESULT_MAX_BYTES`. Two constants join the relay's others, both chosen 2026-10-20 and unsealed: `RELAY_PARENT_POLL_MS = 200` (pi gets its signal within 0.2 s of install's death) and `RELAY_RESULT_MAX_BYTES = 16 MiB` (two streams at main's 1 MiB need 12 MiB after JSON's worst six-byte escape). In `lib/bounded-spawn-child.mjs`, POSIX only, an unref'd interval compares `process.ppid` with `spec.parentPid`; on a change it clears itself and calls `terminate("SIGINT")` only when no termination is in progress, so pi gets SIGINT, the 1 s grace, then the group kill. The deadline, Windows and signal-handler paths are unchanged. nana-setup registers no signal listener, so Ctrl-C now reaches pi through this watch: install dies on the signal, and the relay sees it. Rows R-2130 to R-2133 sit in FEAT-013 SUB-013 after R-2027: CAP-04 moves from 464 to 468 rows, FEAT-013 from 172 to 176 and SUB-013 from 41 to 45. `pi-launch-limits.test.mjs` gains a SIGINT-ignoring switch for the hang fixture, a cleanup delay for the lock fixture, a large-output fixture and the four checks; every win32 skip now returns a skip result, so the runner prints one SKIP line and no PASS. The setup README gains one Idempotence sentence and extends the pi-launch-limits row.

**Evidence.** CI run 39399980825 on draft pull request #120 at 86240f7f (GitHub's merge commit 0825db5e merges 86240f7f into its own ancestor 54f1271f, so the tree tested is 86240f7f's): macOS 176 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP of 178 files (7,887 checks pass); Ubuntu 175 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP (7,826); Windows 161 PASS, 0 FAIL, 17 SKIP (6,817 pass, 109 skip), its skips main's declared ones; install-check passes on macOS and Windows. pi-launch-limits passes 13 on macOS and 13 on Ubuntu, so R-2130, R-2131 and R-2133 pass on Linux, which settles the plan's most-likely-wrong claim. On Windows it prints 8 PASS and 5 SKIP lines: R-2026, R-2027's lock check, R-2130, R-2131 and R-2133 skip with their reasons, and R-2132 passes through a `pi.cmd` fake pi. The seat's wrong-code pairs ran on macOS, Node 22.22.2: 9 of 10 red (record `seat-mutate-output-86240f7f.txt`, commit 8d4783e4). The pair that drops the parent pid turns R-2026 and R-2027 red as well as the new checks, so the old signal checks now rest on the watch. Pair 6 survived, as declared: a watch for a parent of pid 1 acts the same on macOS, where an orphan's parent is pid 1; under a Linux subreaper or a container's init it could differ (inferred, not run). The independent check ran on 86240f7f and HOLDS over 7 probes with no MUST (details under seat items). The trace reads 1,572 rows, 0 off form; map:check reads 340 modules, 0 problems. The seat's record is `docs/reviews/pi-launch-followups-2026-10-20/seat-verify-86240f7f.md`, with the Windows log and the independent check beside it.

**Plan and build.** The seat's plan went to one adversary, which amended it. As first worded, the watch called `terminate("SIGINT")` from a repeating interval; its next tick read as a second Ctrl-C and killed at once, cutting pi's 1 s grace to one 200 ms poll, and no planned check noticed, since R-2027's fake pi cleans up at once. A watch that fires once but ignores a termination in progress (a supervisor signalling install and the relay together) did the same. The fix clears the interval and calls terminate only when none is running; the new R-2133, with a pi that takes two polls to clean up, tells it from both. The adversary also added the SIGINT-ignoring switch, since a fake pi that dies on SIGINT let a watch that never kills pass R-2130 and R-2131. It narrowed the feature sentence and the README to install, since no check kills doctor or the dry run. The plan left bug 1 unbuilt: by pi 1.0.2's source, pi takes its settings lock only inside one synchronous read and write, and a local `pi install` runs no npm, so a pi hung at its limit is outside that section. Bug 5, a stuck relay on Windows leaving cmd and pi, has no check here and stays a residual. A pi gpt-5.6-sol builder built it through pi-worker (one build): 8ec28199. Claude Opus 5.5 (the final reviewer) and Claude Fable 5.1 (the land reviewer) review it, both through review-ledger.

## 2026-10-20 — the mutation runner's lock check no longer races its own starting step

Spend served the current priority's CI legs, where a false red costs a re-run and, on the Windows leg that blocks release, a release. On install-cli-pins' CI run 39386603117, attempt 1, the macOS leg failed the contention check in `packages/nana-pack/tests/mutation-runner.test.mjs` (R-1776, R-1777) with overlapText "5:0". Every other field held: 2,400 acquisitions, every worker exited 0, no lock or marker left. Attempt 2 passed, and install-cli-pins touched no mutation-runner code. The check starts with an unreadable gate lock and a gate exclusivity marker. It lifted the lock first and removed the marker second, so a worker that took the lock in that gap found the marker and recorded an overlap the lock did not cause.

**The change.** Tests only, in the contention block of that one file. The gate marker write and its removal after the lift are gone: the check's `enteredFreshUnreadable` read already fails on any worker that enters while the starting lock stands, so the marker added nothing and left an order to get wrong. In the worker script's EEXIST branch each overlap line now names what the worker found in the marker, `a:b found c:d` for a real overlap or `a:b found ?` when the holder had already left. One comment above the `enteredFreshUnreadable` read says why no marker exists during the gate. `lib/mutation-runner.mjs`, the config, the check's title and its R-1776 and R-1777 markers are unchanged; no row, tunable or tree line moved.

**Evidence.** CI run 39399273061 on draft pull request #117 at 8138f592 (GitHub's merge commit 7482a204 merges 8138f592 into its own ancestor 15703d8d, so the tree tested is 8138f592's): macOS 176 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP of 178 files (7,864 checks pass); Ubuntu 175 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP (7,803); Windows 161 PASS, 0 FAIL, 17 SKIP (6,799 pass, 106 skip), its skips main's declared ones; install-check passes on macOS and Windows. mutation-runner.test.mjs reads 39 pass on macOS (37.8 s) and Ubuntu (19.8 s) and `37 pass, 3 skip  116.7s` on Windows, as on main, with the contention check printing PASS there. None of main's known failures showed. The builder's wrong code in `lib/mutation-runner.mjs` turns the check red both ways: W2 (a fresh unreadable lock not treated as held) with enteredFreshUnreadable true, and W3 (1 in 100 contended publications steal the lock) with overlap text naming what each worker found (`1:1 found 2:0 …`). The plan's load probes ran a standalone copy of the check's gate and worker phase, 8 copies beside 12 busy loops on a 10-core Mac: the planner saw overlaps in 9 of 200 runs with the old order, all 10 lines a first turn that found the gate marker and one of them `5:0`; the adversary saw 2 of 40 (`5:0 found gate`, `2:0 found gate`, `2:1 found gate`) and 0 of 200 with no marker, every run reaching 2,400 acquisitions. The CI attribution stays inferred, since the failing record held no marker content; the new diagnostic makes a repeat prove the cause either way. No seat pairs and no independent check: an ordinary lane. The trace reads 1,563 rows, 0 off form; map:check reads 340 modules, 0 problems. The seat's record is `docs/reviews/mutation-runner-lock-overlap-2026-10-20/seat-verify-8138f592.md`, with the Windows log beside it.

**Plan and build.** The planner's design removed the marker before the lift, with a named pause of four lock retry intervals between the two and a new row pinning that order. One adversary amended it: the marker is redundant, so the lane deletes it, and the pause, the tunable and the row go with it, since they existed only to guard the marker's order (the row also pinned the test's own steps, not a runner promise). While probing, a sibling planner overwrote the adversary's scratch file in the seat's shared scratch folder, so its first runs used the notify-lifecycle-pins planner's temp clone for about 5 minutes; it reverted its edit there, re-ran everything in its own clone, and touched no real repository or home. A Claude Sonnet 5 subagent built it in one build (8f7a91e2); 8138f592 merges main 15703d8d, the pi-probe-timeout land. Claude Opus 5.5 (the final reviewer) reviews it through review-ledger.

**Carried to HANDOFF.**

## 2026-10-20 — tests pin eight promises of the pi seat's compaction handoff that read untested

Spend served the current priority's pi-seat line: nana working in terminal mode for pi with nana-pi on macOS and Windows. The compaction handoff, `nana-handoff`, is one of that seat's extensions. Eight of its FEAT-002 rows read untested. The 2026-10-02 clause audit split R-244 (the store stays `~/.pi/agent/handoffs` when `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` is set) and R-245 (a refused symlinked `handoff.path` journals `handoff_symlink_refused` and warns in the UI) off their parents with no test. The 2026-10-04 EARS batch split R-138 and R-807 (only the exact lowercase `off` marks a non-writer; any other value, or none, behaves as no marker) and R-248 and R-880 (the `.pi/handoff.md` refusal matches in any case, and after resolving the parent's real path); astra's r1 mutations, case-folding the marker and dropping the real-path fallback, left every cited file green. R-830 (no `.gitignore` beside the default store file) was astra's r2 SHOULD, and R-189 (the summary body stays raw payload behind its provenance lines, capped at 8000 UTF-16 code units) carried no evidence at all. Nothing was red: the code meets every row, so this is a pin lane.

**The change.** Tests, rows and the code map only; nana-pack's extensions, lib and scripts are byte-unchanged. Eight new checks, each tagged, run on every platform with no skip; a junction stands in for a folder link on win32. handoff-store gains R-830 in block (b), and an R-244 block that copies the user config into an absolute temp agent folder, points `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` at it, compacts and starts a fresh session.
